candidates.evidence: D 1350.7, G 1580.7 and 2D 2698.2 cm-1 at 514.5 nm. The 2D band is a single Lorentzian (FWHM ~32 cm-1) with I2D/IG ≈ 3.0 in height, which is typical of monolayer graphene. A D' shoulder at 1619.6 cm-1 and I_D/I_G ≈ 0.6 show a moderate defect density.
The 2D band is not split and is narrow, with a high 2D/G ratio. This argues against more than one layer, but a turbostratic stack cannot be fully excluded.
The G band is narrow (14 cm-1) and the 2D band is strong, so heavy oxidation is not supported.

hint_reasoning: No material hint was given. The task is to identify the material from the spectrum alone.

peaks.assignment: D band (defect-activated, breathing mode of sp2 rings, intervalley double-resonance)
peaks.source: Lorentzian fit with linear local baseline; assignment per Ferrari & Basko 2013 and Malard 2009. Peak height ~2190 counts.
Lorentzian fit; assignment per Ferrari 2006. Peak height ~3630 counts.
Two-Lorentzian fit of the G region. It is a weak shoulder, ~327 counts above baseline, so the position and width are less certain. Assignment per Eckmann 2012.

peaks.assignment: 2D (G') band, overtone of D, double resonance
peaks.source: Single Lorentzian fit; assignment per Ferrari 2006. Peak height ~10900 counts.

properties.name: layers
properties.source: A single symmetric Lorentzian 2D band with FWHM ~32 cm-1 and I2D/IG ≈ 3.0 (height; area ratio ≈ 6.8) indicates monolayer graphene (Ferrari 2006). The 2D width is somewhat above the ~25-30 cm-1 of pristine monolayer, probably from defects or inhomogeneity.

properties.name: defect_level
properties.source: I_D/I_G ≈ 0.60 (height) or 0.65 (area), with a visible D' band. The G band stays narrow (14 cm-1), so the sample is in the low-defect-density regime (stage 1 of the Ferrari-Robertson amorphization trajectory, Cançado 2011), not heavily disordered.

properties.name: L_D_nm
properties.value: ~14 (range 13.9-14.5 depending on whether height or area ratio is used)
properties.source: Cançado et al. 2011, Nano Lett. 11, 3190: L_D^2 = (1.8e-9) λ^4 (I_D/I_G)^-1 with λ = 514.5 nm, which gives L_D^2 ≈ 126 nm^2 / 0.6 ≈ 210 nm^2. This corresponds to a defect density of roughly 1.5e11 cm-2. It is valid only for L_D ≳ 3-4 nm, which holds here.

properties.name: defect_type
properties.value: vacancy-like (sp2 point defects) most likely; boundaries or sp3 defects less likely
properties.source: I_D/I_D' ≈ 6.7 (height). Eckmann et al. 2012, Nano Lett. 12, 3925 give ~13 for sp3 defects, ~7 for vacancies and ~3.5 for grain boundaries. The D' shoulder is weak and the ratio uncertain (~±2), so vacancy-type is only a tentative assignment.

properties.name: doping_type
properties.source: G at 1580.7 cm-1 and 2D at 2698 cm-1 are near the values for undoped, unstrained graphene at 514.5 nm. The G width of 14 cm-1 does not suggest strong doping.

properties.name: strain_sign
properties.source: No significant offset from the expected G and 2D positions. The G/2D correlation was not analysed in detail, so only large strain is excluded.

artifacts.type: No cosmic-ray spikes found: robust outlier screening found only noise-level points and peak tops. A smooth, slowly varying luminescence/background is present (about 800 counts at 1100 cm-1 and about 1200 counts near 1700 cm-1, falling to about 530 counts near 3000 cm-1), which was treated as baseline.

citations: Ferrari et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 97, 187401 (2006)
limits: The spectrum stops at 3000 cm-1, so 2D' (~3240) is not covered, and D+D'' (~2450) and D+D' (~2950) are not measurable. D+D' sits on a steep background and was not detected, which is not evidence against defects.
The Si 520.7 cm-1 line is outside the 1100-3000 cm-1 window, so there is no substrate line to report and no internal calibration against Si.

L_D comes from an empirical I_D/I_G relation (Cançado 2011) that assumes point-like defects and the 514.5 nm calibration. It has roughly ±30% or larger uncertainty and depends on how the baseline is subtracted. The estimate does not distinguish the low-defect branch from the high-defect branch, but the narrow G band (14 cm-1) and strong 2D favour the low-defect branch.

The defect type rests on the weak, poorly constrained D' shoulder (~327 counts, about 10% of G). I_D/I_D' ≈ 7 is only suggestive of vacancy-like defects. Mixed defect types cannot be excluded, and the ratio is also affected by doping and laser energy.

Layer number was judged from the single 2D line shape and the intensity ratio only. A twisted or turbostratic bilayer would also give a single 2D peak. Doping and strain cannot be separated without a G-vs-2D position correlation analysis and a calibrated reference.
This is a single spectrum (one spot), so spatial homogeneity is unknown. No polarization dependence was measured, so no polarization pattern is assigned to the peaks.
